issues.issue: Whether 'countries of nationality' in IRPA s.96 includes a country whose citizenship is obtainable only by renouncing another citizenship (certified question)
issues.applicant_position: Minister says s.96 covers a country where citizenship can be obtained, so the Federal Court erred in limiting it to existing citizenship.
issues.respondent_position: Respondent says the case law covers only mere formalities; citizenship is a fundamental right no one should have to renounce.
issues.result_quote: It follows that Pinard J. erred in finding that "countries of nationality," in section 96 of the IRPA, did not include potential countries of nationality.

issues.issue: Whether the respondent's need to renounce Rwandan citizenship makes Ugandan citizenship unavailable to him
issues.applicant_position: Minister says it is within respondent's power to renounce Rwandan and obtain Ugandan citizenship.
issues.respondent_position: Respondent says Ugandan citizenship is conditional on renunciation, so it does not exist at the hearing time.
issues.result_quote: It is, here, within the respondent's power to renounce his Rwandan citizenship and to obtain a Ugandan citizenship.

issues.issue: Whether citizenship being a fundamental right means a claimant cannot be required to renounce it to avoid refugee status
issues.applicant_position: Minister says no one is forced to renounce; the respondent keeps his choice and the consequences of it.
issues.respondent_position: Respondent says citizenship is a fundamental right no one should be compelled to renounce; Chavarria was wrongly decided.
issues.result_quote: This proposition, in my view, is much too broad.
